anya: quick heads-up — marlinx9b canary is seeing sporadic OOMs on Dedicated nodes when the prompt includes long retrieval context (pdf+kb snippets). Repro rate ~1/12 requests.

miguel: thanks, any pattern on batch size / max_new_tokens?

anya: mostly during 3-5 concurrent streams, batch size auto=8. max_new_tokens set by client to 1024 in a few repros. normal client calls < 256.

liam: sounds like memory fragmentation + large generation windows. Did we try lowering continuous batch max or slot reservation?

anya: not yet. Also noticed quality delta when we tried int8 yesterday — a small hallucination increase on QA evals. Could be quant + truncation.

nidhi: @anya can you paste the OOM traceback from the runtime? ops-bot reported GPU OOM on dev-gpu-42.

anya: sure — stack paste below:
```
[2026-03-21T18:14:03Z] GPU-0 OOM: attempted alloc 1.6 GB
serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp: line 233 assert(false) // failed alloc during KV prep
stack: runtime::continuous_batcher -> kv_prefetch -> attention_kernels
requests: prompt_len=640, gen_so_far=1024, batch=6
```

miguel: KV cache blowup — when prompt_len large + max_new_tokens high, per-request KV alloc skyrockets. We should gate max_active_kv per-gpu and trim per-request slot.

liam: propose three quick mitigations for canary: 1) soft-cap max_new_tokens to 512 via inference policy for canary model; 2) reduce continuous_batch.max_batch to 4 for marlinx9b; 3) enable aggressive KV-evict-after-n-requests (n=1) for prefetched long prompts.

anya: I can push a canary override config. Something like:
{
  "model": "marlinx9b",
  "routing": {"canary": true},
  "runtime_overrides": {
    "max_new_tokens_cap": 512,
    "continuous_batch": {"max_batch": 4, "max_latency_ms": 30},
    "kv": {"aggressive_eviction": true}
  }
}

nidhi: also add a per-request allocation guard to fail-fast smaller ones instead of taking large slots. We had similar for phoenix14b.

kari: QA noted the hallucination uptick with int8 — if we reduce max_new_tokens we should re-run the QA evals with the smaller decode window to check net quality change. I can run a focused eval set (100 queries) once canary is stable.

miguel: agreed. Safety first: prefer softer defaults rather than global quant changes. For the quant experiment: leave int8 for now, but add a deterministic warmup that forces small warmstart batches to compact allocator.

liam: small patch to allocator heuristics helped before — will try bumping slot_coalesce_threshold to 0.6 and enabling defrag pass between batches. Patch below:
--- runtime/allocator.cpp
+++ runtime/allocator.cpp
@@ -412,7 +412,9 @@
-    if (free_frac < 0.5) return;
+    // be more aggressive on marlinx9b canary to avoid fragmentation
+    if (model_name == "marlinx9b" && in_canary) free_frac = std::max(free_frac, 0.6);
+    if (free_frac < 0.5) return;
     perform_defrag_pass();

anya: I'll deploy the config override and the allocator tweak to canary nodes after lunch. Rolling in sequence: config -> allocator -> QA evals.

ops-bot: deploy start: canary-config-5501234567 @ 2026-03-21T18:30:00Z :gear:

nidhi: ping me if the revert is needed. Keep logs verbose for first 200 requests.

kari: running evals once deploy stabilizes. I'll compare generation quality and token-level latency before/after.

miguel: if canary holds for 6 hours, we can promote defaults for marlinx9b across Dedicated. Otherwise rollback and try a different quant profile (int8+range-clamp).

anya: noted. thanks all — will update thread when deploy finishes. :thumbsup:

liam: one more ask — can we add a runtime metric for peak_kv_alloc_per_req? would help triage.

nidhi: file a quick ticket? i'll prioritize metric ingestion for dedicated cluster.

anya: filed: INF-9241 — peak_kv_alloc_per_req + canary verbose logs.

ops-bot: deploy complete: canary-config-5501234567 @ 2026-03-21T18:33:10Z :white_check_mark:
